commitResults.messageTitle: HelpCommands: Add command help to both consoles
commitResults.messageBody:
LabLog has no command list or detailed usage guidance at its prompts.
Users must consult external documentation to find command syntax and
examples, and the separate consoles make availability unclear.

Add help to list common Version 1 commands and help COMMAND to show
syntax, fields, and an example. Share one handler between both consoles
so their guidance stays consistent without accessing application records.
Identify which console supports each command and note that loan creation
is not yet connected.

Document help in the README and User Guide, and add tests for command
syntax, console recovery, and unchanged records. Verify the full JUnit
suite and Checkstyle checks with Java 25.

Return help only demonstrates reporting damage, so users must infer how
to return an item without new faults and whether to run both forms.

Add the plain return example and explain the outcome of each form. State
that the examples are alternatives for an active loan so users do not
attempt to return the same loan twice. Exercise both displayed commands
against separate active loans to verify that the examples are usable.

Borrower help shows only one field order and one loan lookup. Users have
no worked example of registering another borrower with reordered fields
or checking that borrower's loans afterwards.

Add a second registration with a distinct ID and reordered prefixes, and
pair each registration with a loan lookup example. Explain the expected
outcome so users can follow the examples in the borrower console. Test
the displayed commands through the handlers to verify that both field
orders register borrowers and both lookups accept their IDs.

The remaining help examples show syntax without explaining prerequisites
or outcomes. Users also lack examples of switching between the command
list and detailed help.

Explain the loan, history, and exit examples, and add examples for help
itself. Keep sample commands separate from their explanations so users
can copy a command without copying descriptive text. Document the richer
examples and retain the notice that loan creation is not yet connected.

Verify the help and history examples through their handlers and console,
and check that viewing examples preserves records in both consoles. Use
a fixed clock for return examples so their checks do not depend on the
current date. Run the full JUnit suite and Checkstyle with Java 25.
HelpCommands: Add command help to both consoles

commitResults.messageTitle: LabLog: Validate prompt input and update guides
commitResults.messageBody:
The main prompt treats unavailable commands as equipment IDs and consumes
subsequent input as equipment details. The guides still contain template
instructions and describe workflows that are not yet connected.

Reject unavailable commands and blank or multi-token asset input before
starting registration. Add regression tests and packaged CLI smoke checks
so command recovery and borrower persistence are verified through the
actual entry points.

Update the README, user and developer guides, and integration notes to
match the current application. Document remaining validation and workflow
gaps, clarify that active-loan lookup does not enforce uniqueness, and
record verification results so passing checks do not imply full lending
support.

Verify 53 JUnit tests, five console smoke tests, both Checkstyle tasks,
and the executable JAR build with Java 25. Check local documentation links
and retain the historical PowerShell transcript unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: LabLog: Add assertions and diagnostic logging
commitResults.messageBody:
Help and prompt validation have no diagnostic logging, and internal
command routing assumptions are not checked with Java assertions.
This makes unexpected control flow harder to diagnose during development.

Add assertions for record-command dispatch and validated asset IDs.
Trace help requests, rejected input, and incomplete registration with
Java logging at FINE level. Use the built-in logger to avoid additional
dependencies and omit raw input from diagnostic messages.

Add opt-in logging configuration and document how to enable assertions
and diagnostics. Update the CLI smoke check to reflect that loan is now
available in the main console.

Verify unit tests, both Checkstyle tasks, the executable JAR build, and
all five CLI smoke tests with Java 25. Check diagnostic output manually
with assertions enabled.
LabLog: Add equipment listing command

commitResults.messageTitle: ﻿Borrower: Support exit in the borrower console
commitResults.messageBody:
The borrower console only accepts EOF to close, unlike the main console.
Users need a discoverable command that ends the session consistently.

Accept exit before dispatching borrower commands and document it in the
startup message, help, and guides. Preserve EOF support and reject exit
with extra arguments. Test that later input is not processed after exit.

Verify all unit tests, Checkstyle, the JAR build, and five CLI smoke tests
with Java 25.

Equipment registration currently requires four answers or closes at EOF.
Allow cancel at every detail prompt and return to the main prompt without
saving a partial record. Keep EOF distinct so exhausted input still exits.
Cover cancellation at all four prompts and successful registration after
cancellation. Document the cancellation word in prompts and the guide.

Verify unit tests, Checkstyle, the JAR build, and five CLI smoke tests
with Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: LabLog: Use a short recurring console prompt
commitResults.messageBody:
The main console repeats full command syntax before every input, hiding
results in prompt text. Show the command summary once at startup and use
a short lablog prompt thereafter. Keep detailed guidance behind help.
Verify that several commands produce one startup summary and one short
prompt per input. This remains usable before the welcome-banner PR lands.

Verify unit tests, Checkstyle, the JAR build, and five CLI smoke tests
with Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Console: Show a consistent versioned welcome
commitResults.messageBody:
The consoles greet differently and do not identify the running release.
Share a welcome renderer showing LabLog v1.0, the console name, purpose,
and a help hint. Keep borrower EOF guidance available until issue #34
lands. Update guides and exact-output tests for the shared presentation.

Merge alongside #30 for a concise prompt with clear startup guidance.
The greeting changes overlap #34; retain its exit guidance when merging.

Verify unit tests, Checkstyle, the JAR build, and five CLI smoke tests
with Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Help: Separate guidance with spacing and rules
commitResults.messageBody:
Help output runs directly into surrounding prompts, making long examples
hard to distinguish. Frame summaries and detailed guidance with blank
lines and dotted ASCII rules in both consoles. Keep error messages short
and preserve copyable example lines. Avoid terminal-specific colour or
cursor escapes so redirected output stays readable.

Verify unit tests, Checkstyle, the JAR build, and five CLI smoke tests
with Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Inventory: Reject duplicate and incomplete units
commitResults.messageBody:
Duplicate asset IDs make later units unreachable, and blank details leave
equipment records incomplete. Validate details when constructing units
and reject duplicate IDs in Inventory before mutation. Reject known IDs
before prompting and recover from invalid details in the main console.
Test preservation of existing records and registration after errors.

The registration recovery edits overlap #29; retain cancellation handling
when merging both changes.

Verify unit tests, Checkstyle, the JAR build, and five CLI smoke tests
with Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Inventory: List equipment with live availability
commitResults.messageBody:
The develop console cannot list equipment or show availability without
knowing an asset ID. Add list with identifying details, location, and
availability derived from current loans. Reflect returns immediately and
handle empty inventory and invalid syntax without modifying records.

PR #43 adds a basic list command on master, which is not yet in develop.
This PR retains its displayed fields and adds the availability required
by #31. Reconcile the two list dispatch paths when syncing master.

Verify unit tests, Checkstyle, the JAR build, and five CLI smoke tests
with Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Loans: List all active loans and overdue status
commitResults.messageBody:
Technicians cannot inspect all outstanding loans from the main console.
Add active-loans with asset ID, borrower ID, due date, and overdue status.
Sort by due date and asset ID, exclude returned loans, and use the shared
clock so loans due today remain on time. Cover empty data, malformed
commands, mixed loan states, and console dispatch with a fixed clock.

Verify unit tests, Checkstyle, the JAR build, and five CLI smoke tests
with Java 25.

The history display supports reservations, faults, and maintenance but
normal sessions cannot create these entries. Add commands for dated notes
on registered units and combine them with loan and caller-supplied history.
Validate dates, equipment, and descriptions before adding entries.

These commands record notes only; they do not change availability or
persist notes across restarts. Document this boundary and test all three
types through the main console as well as invalid-input preservation.

Verify unit tests, Checkstyle, the JAR build, and five CLI smoke tests
with Java 25.

Unknown single words currently start registration, so command typos can
create unintended equipment. Require add and reject other unknown input
with a help hint. Parse all four prefixed fields in any order before
adding a unit, rejecting missing, repeated, unknown, and blank fields.

Retain add ASSET_ID as an explicit wizard entry point so #29 cancellation
remains useful. Update registration examples and integration fixtures.
Merge the wizard tests from #29 with the explicit add prefix when combining
these branches. Retain #35 validation in both registration paths.

Verify unit tests, Checkstyle, the JAR build, and five CLI smoke tests
with Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: LabLog: Share borrower commands in the main console
commitResults.messageBody:
Borrower commands run in a separate process with empty loan records, so
users cannot inspect loans issued by the main console. Route add-borrower
and loans through the main console using its inventory and loan book.
Load the shared borrower file at startup and validate registered borrowers
before lending. Preserve injectable in-memory records for tests.

Verify registration, unknown-borrower rejection, lending, equipment names,
returns, and borrower reload in one workflow. The standalone borrower CLI
remains available. Coordinate the optional data-path argument with #36
when merging persistence, since both changes update startup.

Verify unit tests, Checkstyle, the JAR build, and five CLI smoke tests
with Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Persist equipment and complete loan history
commitResults.messageBody:
Equipment, loans, and returns disappear when the main console exits.
Save them together in a versioned UTF-8 snapshot and reload at startup.
Replace the previous file atomically before confirming a mutation.
Reject corrupt data without overwriting it, and stop the session after a
save failure rather than continue with unconfirmed changes.

Keep injected constructors in memory for tests. Verify Unicode details,
active and returned loans, return faults, corrupt data, save failures,
and a three-process register/lend/return/history workflow.

Use one process per data file. Borrowers and standalone history notes are
outside this snapshot. When combining #33, reconcile its borrower-file
argument with the equipment-data path. When combining #28, call the same
save hook after one-line registration as after wizard registration.

Verify unit tests, Checkstyle, the JAR build, and six CLI smoke tests
with Java 25.

Equipment records cannot currently be viewed together by asset ID, making it difficult to inspect a unit's usage and condition.

Add a history command that combines active and returned loans with supplied reservation, fault, and maintenance entries. Sort records chronologically and connect lookup to the equipment prompt.

Use a shared display format so the remaining features can supply records without coupling their models. Add command and console tests, and document the remaining integration work.

commitResults.messageTitle: Returns: Record equipment returns and faults
commitResults.messageBody:
Loans track a return date but lack a return command and fault details. Users need to close a loan and preserve the condition reported at return.

Add return ASSET_ID with an optional faults/ description. Use the system clock to date returns and validate input before changing the active loan.

Store reported faults on the loan so history reflects the return without duplicating records. Preserve existing callers and leave equipment faults unchanged.

Add return and integration tests, and document usage and limitations. All 37 tests and both Checkstyle checks pass with Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Borrower: Add validated records and persistence
commitResults.messageBody:
LabLog has loan records but no registry of borrower contact details.
Issue #10 needs unique, validated borrowers that survive a restart.

Add immutable borrower records and a borrower book with duplicate-ID
checks and file persistence. Save the proposed state atomically before
updating memory so failed writes do not register unsaved borrowers.

Keep the new classes independent of the pending equipment entry point
so this increment can be reviewed without overlapping PR #16. Add tests
for reloads, duplicate rejection, failed saves, corrupt records, and
immutable snapshots. Command handling follows in a later commit.

Refs #10

commitResults.messageTitle: Borrower: Add registration and loan commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Borrower records can be stored, but technicians have no commands to
register contacts or inspect one borrower's active loans.

Add add-borrower and loans command handlers with strict field validation,
duplicate rejection, and active-loan listings ordered by due date and
asset ID. Determine overdue status using the supplied local clock.

Reuse the existing loan book and accept an equipment-name lookup to keep
these handlers compatible with the pending inventory implementation.
Provide a standalone console until the shared prompt is integrated.

Add tests for command syntax, contact validation, duplicate registration,
loan filtering and ordering, local-date boundaries, and console recovery.

Refs #10, #11

commitResults.messageTitle: Test: Add borrower console regression checks
commitResults.messageBody:
JUnit covers borrower handlers, but it does not launch the standalone
console twice to verify that registrations survive a process restart.

Add a PowerShell 7 runner and a recorded plan for registration, duplicate
rejection, empty loan listings, and borrower reloads. Use a fresh data
file per run and compare output exactly after normalizing line endings.
Stop on the first failure and record the console session for review.

Keep final prompt spaces in comparisons while omitting them from the
Markdown display. Record passing results from both Java 25 processes.

Refs #10, #11

The README still describes the Duke template and gives no instructions

Document Java 25 setup, borrower command syntax, validation, persistence,

Replace the old demo instructions with runnable borrower examples.

commitResults.messageTitle: Loan: Add loan records and their storage
commitResults.messageBody:
LabLog can register equipment units but has no way to record who
borrowed a unit or when it is due back, so staff cannot tell which
units are currently out.

Add Loan to represent one borrowing record and LoanBook to hold them.
Reference the borrower by identifier instead of by object so that loans
can be recorded before borrower records exist (#10), and derive
availability from these records instead of storing a status field on
each equipment unit, which would have to be kept in sync on every loan
and return.

The loan command is not wired up yet because it needs the Inventory
introduced by #8.

commitResults.messageTitle: LoanBook: Add active loan lookup for a unit
commitResults.messageBody:
Lending out a unit that is already with a borrower would create two
active loans for the same unit, and LabLog has no way to notice that
today.

Add findActiveLoan to return the loan currently holding a unit, and
hasActiveLoan as a shorthand for callers that only need a yes or no.
Return an Optional rather than null so the caller cannot forget the
available case, and return the loan itself so the warning can name the
borrower and the due date.

The warning message belongs to the loan command, which still needs the
Inventory from #8.
LabLog: Validate prompt input and update guides

commitResults.messageTitle: Loan: Connect the loan command to the main console
commitResults.messageBody:
LabLog could store loans but had no way to create one: help listed the
loan command as "not yet connected", and typing it at the prompt was
treated as an asset ID, which started registering a bogus equipment
unit. Nothing could be returned or shown in history either, because no
loan could exist.

Add LoanCommands to parse "loan ASSET_ID b/BORROWER_ID d/DUE_DATE" as
documented in help, and dispatch it from LabLog alongside history and
return. Every check runs before the record is stored, so a rejected
command leaves no partial loan. Warn instead of lending a unit that is
already out, naming the borrower and the due date, which is what #13
asks for.

Borrower identifiers are accepted as given. The main console does not
hold borrower records yet, so checking them belongs with the #10 and
#11 integration; the help text now says so rather than claiming loans
are unconnected.

commitResults.messageTitle: LabLog: Allow the loan command in the main console
commitResults.messageBody:
Validating prompt input (#24) and connecting the loan command landed at
the same time and disagree: the main prompt now rejects loan as a
command that belongs to another console, while the loan command is in
fact dispatched there.

Drop loan from the rejected list, keeping loans and add-borrower, which
really are borrower-console commands. Replace the loan cases in
run_unavailableCommands_rejectsWithoutConsumingEquipmentDetails with a
test that issues a loan through the console, so the original concern
that a command must never start an equipment registration is still
covered.

The test uses a due date far in the future because this entry point
dates loans from the system clock.

commitResults.messageTitle: Docs: Record that the loan command is connected
commitResults.messageBody:
The guides were written while loan creation was unavailable, so they
still tell readers that no console can issue a loan. The user guide also
quotes the output of help loan, which no longer matches what the program
prints.

Update the three README files and both guides to describe the command as
working, refresh the quoted help output, and add a user guide section and
a developer guide section for it. The user guide gains a command summary
row, and the developer guide records that LoanCommands, not LoanBook, is
where duplicate active loans are prevented.

Leave the borrower limitation in place: the main console holds no
BorrowerBook, so borrower IDs are still unchecked, and the guides now say
that rather than saying loans cannot be issued. The note that the
standalone borrower console cannot issue loans also stays, because that
console is unchanged.

Do not touch test/verification-report.md. It records a verification run
against a named revision, so it describes what was true at that revision.
